bare/ask: Say you want to package GNU Hello, a small C program, using only the derivation you know.
bare/tools: The sandbox starts nearly empty. So you must hand it a compiler, make, tar, sed, grep, awk and more, each by its store path.
bare/steps: Then you spell out every step yourself: unpack, configure, compile, install.
bare/again: And the next C program needs all of it again. Thousands of packages, repeating the same lines.
wrap/stdenv: Nix packages, the big collection of package recipes, has a fix. Its standard environment, standard env, bundles a compiler, make and the small tools, with a script that knows the usual steps.
wrap/call: Its function make derivation takes an attribute set and calls derivation for you. What comes back is still an ordinary derivation.
wrap/name: P name and version join up into the name, hello dash two point twelve.
wrap/src: source says where the code comes from. fetch U R L downloads it, and the hash says exactly what must arrive.
wrap/native: Two lists name your dependencies. native build inputs holds programs the build runs, like package config. They go on path during the build.
wrap/link: build inputs holds what the result links against, like zlib. The compiler is told where to find it.
phases/order: That script runs a build in phases, always in the same order. Unpack, patch, configure, build, check, install, fixup.
phases/dance: The defaults are the classic Unix dance: dot slash configure, then make, then make install.
phases/out: Configure is told to install under dollar out, so make install lands in your store path.
phases/fixup: Fixup tidies the result: it strips binaries, and points scripts at interpreters in the store.
phases/over: When a default is wrong for your package, set that phase yourself. Two single quotes start a multi-line string, and this one replaces make install.
phases/mk: Your commands have the same duty as any builder: put the result in dollar out.
callpackage/fn: A package file does not reach out for what it needs. It is a function: it takes its dependencies as arguments, and returns a derivation.
callpackage/set: Nix packages is one enormous attribute set, with every package under its name.
callpackage/call: call package reads the names the function asks for, finds each one in that set, and passes it in.
callpackage/over: The empty set at the end is for your own choices. Name an argument there, and your value wins over nix packages.
callpackage/knot: Notice that hello sits in the same set it takes its arguments from. The set refers to itself.
callpackage/lazy: Laziness is what makes that work. Asking for hello works out only what hello needs, and the rest of the set stays unevaluated.
